 Titre du poste: Directeur, PMO et excellence opérationnelle
 À propos de Pratt & Whitney Canada 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada (P&WC) est un leader mondial de l’innovation aérospatiale, dont le siège social est situé à Longueuil, au Québec, depuis 1928. Nous concevons et fabriquons des moteurs d’aéronefs de nouvelle génération qui propulsent la plus grande flotte mondiale d’avions et d’hélicoptères dans les segments de l’aviation d’affaires, de l’aviation générale et de l’aviation régionale.
 Depuis près de 100 ans, nos équipes sont à l’avant-garde des technologies de propulsion, repoussant les limites afin de rendre nos moteurs plus performants et fiables. Nos moteurs soutiennent des missions essentielles, du transport de passagers et de marchandises aux services médicaux d’urgence, aux opérations humanitaires et à la lutte contre les feux de forêt, partout dans le monde.
 Un employeur de choix 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada a été reconnue comme l’un des meilleurs employeurs au Canada en 2026 selon Forbes, et ce, pour une 11e année consécutive. L’entreprise s’est également classée au premier rang des employeurs de l’industrie de l’aérospatiale et de la défense au pays. De plus, notre siège social figure toujours parmi les meilleurs employeurs de la région de Montréal. Ensemble, ces distinctions confirment notre réputation d’employeur de choix à Montréal, au Canada et à l’échelle mondiale.
 Pourquoi rejoindre notre équipe? 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada est à la recherche d’un leader transformationnel pour occuper le poste de Directeur, PMO et excellence opérationnelle. Agissant comme le principal partenaire stratégique du directeur exécutif des technologies numériques, cette personne assurera une maîtrise rigoureuse, une visibilité complète et une exécution disciplinée de l’ensemble du portefeuille de projets numériques de P&WC. Il ne s’agit pas d’un rôle traditionnel de suivi de projets, mais d’un poste de leadership stratégique responsable de l’exécution, de la gouvernance, de la santé financière et de l’amélioration continue d’un portefeuille de transformation numérique de plusieurs millions de dollars. 
 En supervisant des initiatives complexes dans les domaines de l’ingénierie, de la fabrication, de la chaîne d’approvisionnement, des services après-vente et des fonctions corporatives, le directeur jouera un rôle de liaison essentiel entre P&WC, les organisations de livraison basées en Pologne et le PMO mondial de Pratt & Whitney. En intégrant la responsabilité financière et l’excellence opérationnelle au cadre de gestion du PMO, cette personne veillera à ce que les investissements technologiques stratégiques génèrent une valeur mesurable pour les résultats financiers et une transformation durable de l’entreprise.
 Le poste s’effectue à notre établissement de Longueuil , du lundi au vendredi, selon des horaires flexibles et exclusivement en présentiel.
 À quoi ressemblera votre quotidien? 
 1. Partenariat exécutif et gouvernance du portefeuille
 Leadership opérationnel: Agir à titre de principal leader opérationnel des technologies numériques au Canada, en gérant les priorités concurrentes et en favorisant une étroite harmonisation entre les différentes unités d’affaires et régions géographiques.
 Maturité du PMO: Définir et mettre en œuvre une stratégie pluriannuelle pour le PMO, en établissant des modèles opérationnels robustes, des cadres de gouvernance et des indicateurs de performance favorisant une exécution cohérente du portefeuille.
 Stratégie d’investissement: Collaborer avec la direction pour identifier, prioriser et gérer l’allocation des fonds aux investissements technologiques stratégiques, tout en maintenant une feuille de route régionale de transformation numérique.
 Visibilité exécutive: Mettre en place des tableaux de bord automatisés et des systèmes de gestion au sein de l’écosystème régional de gestion de portefeuille de projets (PPM), afin de fournir à la direction une visibilité en temps réel sur la santé du portefeuille, les risques et les résultats d’affaires.
 2. Gestion et exécution de programmes complexes
 Gestion de bout en bout: Diriger un portefeuille complexe de programmes de transformation à l’échelle de l’entreprise, en assurant la planification des ressources, la gestion des interdépendances interfonctionnelles et la résolution rapide des obstacles.
 Envergure organisationnelle: Assurer la réalisation sans faille de programmes majeurs et essentiels aux activités de l’entreprise, notamment en matière de gestion du cycle de vie des produits (PLM), de planification des ressources de l’entreprise (ERP), de systèmes d’exécution de la fabrication (MES), de modernisation infonuagique et de plateformes de données et d’analytique.
 Méthodologies de livraison: Promouvoir les meilleures pratiques en matière de méthodologies de gestion et de livraison de projets (Agile, SAFe, Waterfall et hybrides), et assurer l’application uniforme des pratiques de contrôle des projets et d’assurance qualité.
 3. Excellence opérationnelle et réalisation de la valeur financière
 Rigueur financière: Superviser la budgétisation, les prévisions et la gestion des investissements du portefeuille. Collaborer avec les équipes financières pour établir un suivi rigoureux du rendement des investissements (ROI), de la réalisation des bénéfices et des écarts.
 Optimisation des processus: Harmoniser et optimiser les processus dans Planview afin d’éliminer les inefficacités, d’accélérer les délais de livraison et de surveiller les principaux indicateurs de santé opérationnelle.
 Amélioration continue: Diriger des initiatives visant à améliorer la prévisibilité et à accélérer la mise en marché, en intégrant les principes du RTX Operating System à l’ensemble des activités d’exécution et d’amélioration du portefeuille.
 4. Leadership du changement et développement des capacités organisationnelles
 Développement des talents: Développer, encadrer et diriger une organisation PMO performante composée de gestionnaires de projets, de gestionnaires de programmes, de Scrum Masters et de leaders en transformation.
 Intégration mondiale: Diriger la planification des ressources et l’optimisation des capacités entre les organisations de livraison au Canada et en Pologne, en comblant les lacunes en matière de compétences par le recours stratégique à des ressources externes et au recrutement.
 Adoption par les utilisateurs: Assumer la responsabilité du cadre de gestion du changement pour les déploiements à grande échelle, en faisant évoluer l’approche du PMO au-delà de la mise en service (go-live) pour mettre l’accent sur l’adoption réelle par les utilisateurs et le succès après la mise en œuvre.
 Gestion des parties prenantes: Établir des partenariats solides et fondés sur la confiance avec les équipes d’ingénierie, d’opérations, de chaîne d’approvisionnement, de MRO, de finances et de cybersécurité, afin d’assurer un soutien actif de la direction à l’ensemble des initiatives.
 5. Gouvernance des risques et conformité à l’échelle de l’entreprise
 Atténuation proactive: Diriger l’identification des risques systémiques liés au portefeuille, la planification des mesures d’atténuation et les processus d’escalade auprès de la direction afin de protéger les échéanciers stratégiques.
 Conformité et audits: Veiller à ce que l’ensemble des cadres de livraison du PMO respecte rigoureusement les normes de conformité de l’industrie aérospatiale, les politiques corporatives, les exigences en matière de cybersécurité, les principes de gouvernance des données et les contrôles d’audit interne.
 Ce poste s’inscrit dans un milieu de travail francophone, néanmoins il nécessite une très bonne connaissance de l’anglais pour lire et comprendre, sur une base quotidienne, de la documentation et des termes techniques qui peuvent émaner d’organisations internationales, ainsi que pour écrire et communiquer en anglais avec des clients, des fournisseurs ou des collègues internationaux.
 Qu’est-ce qu’il vous faut pour réussir? 
 Baccalauréat en technologies de l’information, en génie, en administration des affaires, en informatique ou dans un domaine connexe.
 Plus de 14 ans d’expérience progressive en technologies numériques, en gestion de programmes, en leadership PMO ou en transformation organisationnelle.
 Expérience approfondie dans la direction de portefeuilles de projets d’envergure, la gestion de budgets de plusieurs millions de dollars et la réalisation de programmes de transformation numérique.
 Expérience démontrée dans la mise en place et la gestion de PMO au sein de l’industrie aérospatiale, de l’aviation, de la fabrication de pointe ou d’autres secteurs complexes et fortement réglementés.
 Excellentes aptitudes en leadership exécutif et capacité éprouvée à influencer les dirigeants, à résoudre les conflits et à favoriser le consensus au sein d’organisations matricielles réparties géographiquement.
 Certification PMP (Project Management Professional).
 Certification PgMP (Program Management Professional) et/ou PfMP (Portfolio Management Professional).
 Certification SAFe Program Consultant (SPC) ou SAFe Agilist.
 Certifications en gestion de projets Agile.
 Certification Lean Six Sigma.
 Qualifications privilégiées 
 Maîtrise en administration des affaires (MBA), en systèmes d’information, en génie ou dans un domaine connexe.
 Expérience approfondie dans le soutien aux initiatives de transformation en ingénierie, en fabrication, en chaîne d’approvisionnement et dans les services après-vente.
 Expérience démontrée dans des modèles de livraison mondiaux et dans la gestion de relations avec des fournisseurs et partenaires multinationaux.
 Bonne connaissance pratique des méthodologies RTX Operating System, des concepts d’architecture d’entreprise et des principes de gouvernance des données.
 Ce que nous offrons 
 Programme d’assurance collective
 Possibilités d’avancement (progression de carrière)
 Programme de mérite ou programme de reconnaissance
 Club récréatif et sportif
 Garderies à proximité
 Travailler chez Pratt & Whitney Canada 
 Chez Pratt & Whitney Canada, nous allions avec passion, audace et rigueur pour concevoir, fabriquer et entretenir les moteurs d’aéronefs les plus avancés et les plus fiables au monde. Notre travail et la qualité de nos produits contribuent au succès de nos clients, qui à leur tour sauvent des vies, soutiennent le commerce, connectent les communautés et protègent les libertés.

 Job Title: Director, PMO & Operational Excellence
 About Pratt & Whitney Canada 
 An Employer of Choice 
 Why join our team? 
 Pratt & Whitney Canada is seeking a transformational leader to serve as the Director of PMO & Operational Excellence. Acting as the strategic right-hand man to the Executive Director of Digital Technology, this leader will maintain absolute control, visibility, and execution rigor across P&WC’s enterprise digital portfolio. 
 This is not a traditional tracking role. It is a strategic leadership position accountable for the execution, governance, financial health, and continuous improvement of a multimillion-dollar digital transformation portfolio. Overseeing complex initiatives across engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, aftermarket services, and corporate functions, the Director will serve as the critical bridge between P&WC, Poland-based delivery organizations, and the Pratt & Whitney Global PMO. By integrating financial accountability and operational excellence into the PMO framework, this leader ensures our strategic technology investments deliver measurable bottom-line value and sustainable business transformation.
 The position is based at our Longueuil location, from Monday to Friday, with flexible hours and exclusively on-site.
 1. Executive Partnership & Portfolio Governance
 Operational Lead: Act as the primary operational leader for Digital Technology Canada, navigating competing priorities and facilitating tight alignment across diverse business units and geographies.
 PMO Maturation: Define and execute a multi-year PMO strategy, establishing robust operating models, governance frameworks, and performance metrics that drive consistent portfolio execution.
 Investment Strategy: Partner with executive leadership to identify, prioritize, and manage funding allocations for strategic technology investments, maintaining a regional digital transformation roadmap.
 Executive Visibility: Implement automated dashboards and management systems within the regional Project Portfolio Management (PPM) ecosystem to provide real-time executive insights into portfolio health, risks, and business outcomes.
 2. Complex Program Delivery & Execution
 End-to-End Management: Direct a complex portfolio of enterprise transformation programs, driving resource planning, cross-functional dependency management, and rapid blocker resolution.
 Enterprise Scale: Ensure the flawless delivery of large-scale, business-critical programs, including Product Lifecycle Management (PLM), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Cloud modernization, and Data/Analytics platforms.
 Delivery Methodologies: Champion best-in-class project delivery methodologies (Agile, SAFe, Waterfall, Hybrid) and ensure consistent application of project controls and quality assurance practices.
 3. Operational Excellence & Financial Value Realization
 Financial Rigor: Oversee portfolio budgeting, forecasting, and investment management. Partner with finance to establish strict ROI tracking, benefits realization, and variance analysis.
 Process Optimization: Align and optimize processes within Planview to eliminate waste, accelerate delivery timelines, and monitor key operational health metrics.
 Continuous Improvement: Drive initiatives that enhance predictability and speed to market, integrating RTX Operating System principles into all portfolio execution and improvement activities.
 4. Change Leadership & Organizational Capability
 Talent Development: Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing PMO organization consisting of project managers, program managers, Scrum Masters, and transformation leaders.

 Tu rêves avant tout d'une aventure hors du commun dans la nature et un environnement typique québécois ? Tu es cuisinier polyvalent et tu veux troquer ta ville pour la forêt, les lacs et la vraie nature québécoise ? Un poste où tu ne seras pas un numéro, mais un membre à part entière d'une équipe familiale, au cœur de l'une des plus belles régions du Québec. 
 À propos de l'employeur 
 S'installer au Canada, ce n'est pas juste changer de pays. C'est aussi choisir un cadre de vie qui sort complètement de l'ordinaire.
 Ici, c'est l'une des meilleures pourvoiries de Charlevoix et du Fjord du Saguenay, une pourvoirie à droits exclusifs avec 10 chalets et une auberge forestière.  Tu es le cuisinier polyvalent de la maison : bistro et snack le midi, table d'hôte le soir. Menu traditionnel et créations maison sont au programme.

 ● Maintenir un poste de travail propre et organisé.

 ● Respecter les normes d'hygiène et de salubrité.

 ● Tu es polyvalent et à l'aise aussi bien en service rapide qu'en table d'hôte.
 ● Tu es organisé, propre et rigoureux dans ton poste.
 ● Tu as un bel esprit de cohésion d'équipe.
 ● Tu es à l'aise avec l'éloignement : la pourvoirie est située à 1h30 d'une grande ville.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Core is the heart of the MaintainX CMMS: the work orders, planning and scheduling, inventory and parts, reporting, and asset hierarchy that frontline teams touch every day. It is also where some of our newest investment is happening, including two newly formed teams building a Work Execution Platform and a rebuilt Technician Experience from scratch. If you want to work close to what customers use daily, and have a chance at green-field ownership, this is the place.

TEAMS YOU MIGHT JOIN

 - Planners: Planner and scheduler workflows, plus Operating Hours.

 - Inventory Management / Parts: Spare parts, purchase orders, forecasting and vendors.

 - Home / Reporting: The Overview screen, plus shared and scheduled reports.

 - Work Execution Platform: The work order primitives the product runs on: recurrence, assignment, calendar, procedures, automations and permits.

 - Technician Experience: GPS check-in, field UX and offline state for technicians in the field.

 - Enterprise Data Management: Global, multi-site platform capabilities, templates, asset hierarchy and location, and dynamic asset forms.
   
   

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 - Build and improve the workflows customers use every day, from scheduling and parts management to reporting.

 - Solve hard product problems: dense, data-heavy interfaces, large datasets, offline behaviour and multi-site scale.

 - On our newly formed teams, shape architecture and engineering practices from the ground up.

 - Make complex workflows feel simple on desktop and mobile.

THE ROLE

 - Ship features end to end, from planning through production.

 - Partner directly with Product Managers and Designers to shape your team's roadmap, not just execute against it.

 - Own a feature area or system's long-term health: reliability, performance, and the parts of the codebase nobody notices until they break.

 - Review code and mentor other developers on your team.

 - Raise the bar on tooling, testing, and delivery practices.

Our core stack is TypeScript, React, Node.js, and MySQL. Some teams use C# or Python. You don't need to already know every piece of it to apply. You'll land on a team of 5 to 10 people and take on-call rotation as part of the role. Within your first 6 months, you'll own a feature area or system outright.

WHERE WE WORK

We don't have a minimum in-office mandate, but we prefer our teams to be located around our office hubs. In Canada this includes: Montreal and Toronto.

WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 5+ years of professional experience building full-stack web or mobile products.

 - Deep hands-on experience with TypeScript, React, and Node.js.

 - Experience with mobile-first, responsive, iterative development.

 - A track record of writing maintainable, testable code you're comfortable handing off to someone else.

 - Strong written and verbal communication: you can explain a technical tradeoff to a designer or a support lead as easily as to another developer.

 - Comfort making progress on a problem before the spec is fully settled, adjusting as you learn more.

 - Day-to-day use of AI tools in your development workflow, not just occasional experimentation.

 - Nice to have: GraphQL, React Native, or SQL database experience. For this area, we also value: Experience with scheduling or calendar UIs, data-heavy front ends, offline-first or sync architectures, multi-tenant or enterprise platforms, workflow engines, or inventory and transactional systems.

WHAT’S THE JOB? 
 Reporting to the Camp/Lodge and Facilities Manager, the Storekeeper/Inventory Control Clerk is responsible for the effective management of all materials and inventory across on-site and off-site locations. This includes receiving, storing, tracking, and controlling supplies related to food, beverages, chemicals, maintenance, janitorial, housekeeping, and commissary services.
This position is ideally suited for individuals with a background in hospitality or food and beverage, especially those with experience in cost control, inventory management, and supply chain coordination in hotels, camps, or remote operations. The Storekeeper plays a crucial role in supporting day-to-day operations in a remote Arctic mining environment, ensuring efficiency, cost awareness, and service excellence. This position requires fly-in/fly-out travel from Edmonton, Alberta or Yellowknife, Northwest Territories, to the project site in Nunavut, with potential for weather-related delays or logistical challenges.
 The position involves a remote work lifestyle in a Nunavut camp setting with the following working conditions and amenities: 
 All meals and shared accommodations are provided 
 Travel is provided to and from the site locations from a designated hub location in Edmonton, AB
 Access to Wi-Fi 
 Access to laundry facilities and detergents 
 Access to a gym and common areas 
 Requires the operation of pallet jacks and the movement of heavy inventory safely using manual and mechanical jacks. 
 Manual movement of food and other product for the majority of a 12 hour shift in outdoor conditions in all weather conditions.
 Extended periods away from home; rotational schedule required.
 Must comply with all safety and sanitation standards established by the client and company.
 Your work will include: 
 Maintain optimal stock levels and records of inventory (including food, supplies, consumables, chemicals, and MRO—maintenance, repair, and operations) using both warehouse/inventory software and manual tracking methods.
 Monitor for all camp departments, including catering, janitorial, maintenance, and housekeeping.
 Follow FIFO (First-In, First-Out) protocols to reduce spoilage and ensure stock freshness. Conduct routine stock counts and prepare detailed reports on inventory usage, variances, and trends to ensure accurate and up-to-date information.
 Supervise expiration dates and coordinate the timely usage of perishable goods. Receive, document, and organize all shipments in accordance with safety and storage standards.
 Manage and stock commissary items and vending machines, including ordering and pricing.
 Assist with stock movements between sea-cans, warehouses, and various camp locations.
 Prepare consumption and cost analysis reports for food, beverages, water, and maintenance items.
 Apply best practices in F&B cost control to ensure minimal waste and optimized pricing strategies.
 Maintain clean, organized, and safe workspaces; promptly report hazards or incidents. Support and collaborate with hospitality operations, including kitchen and service teams to ensure seamless service and supply flow across departments. Help coordinate the movement of products between sea-cans, site transfers and warehouses.
 Physical Demands: 
 Lift, carry, push, or pull up to 50 lbs
 Climb ladders and stairs
 Stand, walk, squat, kneel or sit according to task for extended lengths of time
 Perform repetitive hand work requiring full use of both hands
 Work with arms above shoulder height
 Requires the operation of pallet jacks and the movement of heavy inventory safely using manual and mechanical jacks. 
 Manual movement of food and other product for the majority of a 12 hour shift in outdoor conditions in all weather conditions.
WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR? 
 Other Skills and Competencies: 
 Proven background in hospitality, hotel, remote camp, or food & beverage operations, particularly in inventory or cost control roles.
 Excellent attention to detail and accuracy in documentation and stock control.
 Strong analytical and financial tracking skills for cost reporting and waste reduction.
 Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and inventory/POS systems.
 Excellent communication and team collaboration skills.
 Cultural awareness and the ability to work respectfully with Indigenous and Inuit team members.
 Required Qualifications: 
 High school diploma or equivalent (post-secondary in hospitality, logistics, or supply chain is an asset).
 Minimum 3 years of experience in inventory or storekeeping roles, preferably in hospitality, camps, or industrial/remote environments.
 Valid driver’s license.
 WHMIS, food
WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU? 
 Enjoy excellent work-life balance with a 4 week on/2 week off rotation or similar
 Ability to expand skills in a large camp atmosphere 
 Work schedule and remuneration: 
 Inventory Control Clerks work on a rotational schedule of 4 weeks on/2 weeks off or similar. Site locations are in remote settings, requiring either air travel to site, or via ground on our shuttle. You may be required to work nights, weekdays, weekends, and general holidays. Wages are paid on an hourly basis and include a starting rate of $25.75.

 Responsabilités

Vous vous joindrez à l'équipe des consultants en solutions de MaintainX à titre de partenaire technique de nos directeurs de comptes du marché intermédiaire. L'équipe prend en charge tout ce qui est technique entre le premier appel et la signature du contrat : découverte, démonstrations, appels d'offres, questionnaires, essais et validation technique.

 Résumé du poste 
 Le poste de Chef, Établissement stratégique des prix consiste à diriger l’établissement des prix pour un ou plusieurs secteurs thérapeutiques (ST) attitrés, en élaborant et en mettant en œuvre la stratégie de prix tout au long du cycle de vie des produits, du lancement et des nouvelles indications jusqu’à l’arrivée des produits génériques. La personne titulaire collabore étroitement avec l’Accès au marché du ST, l’Économie de la santé, les Finances, les Affaires juridiques et l’équipe mondiale afin de protéger l’accès des patients et la valeur commerciale, tout en respectant les exigences du CEPMB et des payeurs. Elle contribue également aux capacités communes d’établissement des prix qui soutiennent tous les ST.
 Responsabilités principales
 Stratégie de prix : Assumer la responsabilité des évaluations de prix pour les actifs attitrés, y compris les options de prix, les scénarios, les analyses de sensibilité et les répercussions sur les prix de liste et nets, et recommander une position de prix.
 Analyses de rentabilité et modélisation des ententes : Diriger l’apport de l’établissement des prix aux analyses de rentabilité de l’accès, y compris la modélisation des prix nets et des ententes, les analyses comparatives et les hypothèses clés; assurer une vigilance à l’égard des prix des produits concurrents et de la réglementation sur les prix afin qu’AbbVie occupe une position concurrentielle, tout en respectant des pratiques d’établissement des prix conformes.
 Négociations avec les payeurs : Élaborer les volets d’établissement des prix de la préparation des négociations avec les payeurs publics et privés, y compris les offres et les contre-offres, l’économie des ententes et les paramètres de négociation; appuyer la direction dans les négociations stratégiques.
 Contrats et conditions commerciales : Examiner les prix et les conditions commerciales dans les lettres d’intention (LI), les ententes d’inscription de produits (EIP), les modifications et les renouvellements.
 Gouvernance et conformité : Gérer les risques liés aux prix, les remontées d’information, les dossiers d’approbation et la mise en œuvre conformément aux exigences du CEPMB et aux politiques internes.
 Gouvernance mondiale des prix : Gérer les processus internes d’approbation des prix et de gouvernance mondiale pour les actifs attitrés; travailler en étroite collaboration avec l’équipe mondiale de l’Établissement des prix pour assurer l’harmonisation avec les directives mondiales d’établissement des prix et le développement des analyses de rentabilité.
 Soutien relatif au CEPMB : Appuyer les obligations de déclaration auprès du CEPMB et toute enquête sur d’éventuels revenus excessifs, en fournissant des données et des analyses sur les prix.

 Gestion des produits génériques et du cycle de vie : Mettre à jour les scénarios d’impact sur les prix lors du lancement de produits génériques et collaborer avec les Finances à l’évaluation de l’incidence sur les prévisions.
 Planification du ST : Agir à titre de personne-ressource unique responsable de l’établissement des prix pour le ST; contribuer à la planification du ST, au plan à long terme et au plan annuel.
 Collaboration : Travailler de façon interfonctionnelle avec l’Accès au marché, l’Économie de la santé, les Finances, les Affaires juridiques, l’équipe mondiale et les Opérations, et établir des relations de travail positives avec les fonctions internes et les bureaux mondiaux et régionaux d’AbbVie; respecter les transferts de dossiers, les décisions et les échéances; contribuer aux outils, aux processus et aux pratiques exemplaires d’établissement des prix communs à tous les ST, et appuyer ses collègues durant les périodes de pointe.

About Jetson 
 Who You Are: 
 Someone who thrives in ambiguity. Early-stage companies don’t hand you a spec and walk away. You’re comfortable defining problems as much as solving them, and you’ve learned to make good decisions with incomplete information. 
 A systems thinker at the hardware-software boundary. You find satisfaction in making complex systems work reliably (and you know how to apply Gall’s Law to get there). When debugging an issue, you naturally consider how all the pieces connect and interact. You’re drawn to the intersection of hardware and software, where the abstractions are thinner and the consequences of your decisions are more tangible. 
 An empathetic collaborator. You enjoy working with hardware engineers on bring-up, backend teams on device-to-server communication, field ops on diagnostics, customer support on real-world issues, and more. You communicate clearly across these boundaries, and you remember that at the end of the day we all succeed or fail together. 
 What We Need: 
 End-to-end ownership of device firmware. Our Jetson Hub and Jetson Thermostat control heat pumps, water heaters, EV chargers, and other home comfort & energy devices, and the magic is in their software. These aren’t disposable gadgets: our devices need to run reliably for 10+ years in homes across the continent. 
 Embedded systems depth. Production C or C++ on microcontrollers. Experience with communication protocols (Modbus, BLE, Wifi, LoRa), memory management, and real-time constraints. Comfort debugging hardware-software interactions. 
 Engineering rigour. Tests, code review, and CI/CD are table stakes–practices which are often treated as optional in firmware. Not at Jetson. 
 Designing for resiliency. Think through failure modes before writing code, but assume the device will encounter unanticipated conditions anyway. Design for diagnostics, graceful degradation, and self-healing recovery paths: we should never have to roll a truck to fix a software bug. 
 Comfort with on-call responsibility. Our customers rely on our systems to heat & cool their homes. When production issues arise, we need engineers who can quickly diagnose, resolve, and ensure they don’t happen again. 
 How You Will Grow: 
 Develop expertise in high-reliability, long-lived systems. Most IoT devices are toys, and most high-reliability software ships once and never changes. Not at Jetson: we keep homes comfortable and safe while pushing new features. You’ll learn to build resilient software that survives a decade in the field and evolves along the way. 
 See the full picture, and influence it. Firmware at Jetson touches hardware, cloud infrastructure, energy markets, end customers, and more. You’ll gain context that’s rare for firmware engineers, with the opportunity to expand into adjacent areas if you’re interested. 
 Shape how we build . We’re a small team building our practices as we go. You’ll help shape our firmware architecture, tooling, and standards, including how we use AI to move faster than ever.

In 1954, Eero Saarinen designed a branch office with glass walls, no offices, and a completely open floor plan in Columbus, Indiana. It was surrounded by trees; the furniture was made by Herman Miller; the lobby flooring was thick, rustic brick. It was built with transparency and community at its core. Since then, a lot of things have happened — Saarinen's branch is now a conference center, people increasingly live on the internet, and it's hard to think of a single financial institution that still applies design thinking to their company.
 Mercury is on a mission to defy those expectations. We're a financial technology company that helps startups spend less time banking* and more time building. We believe that the key to our success revolves around thoughtful design — and we hold the craft of that design to an exceptionally high standard. We're looking for a Staff Brand Designer who sets that bar: someone whose eye is so precise, and whose execution is so considered, that the work around them gets better just by virtue of their presence.
 This is a role for a designer who sweats the details that most people don't notice — the type hierarchy, the negative space, the grid, the crop. Someone who has developed a genuine aesthetic philosophy over years of doing hard work at a high level, and who brings that philosophy to everything they touch.  Set and uphold the craft standard for Mercury's brand — across campaigns, web, social, events, and every surface the brand touches.
 Lead the most technically complex and high-visibility brand design projects end-to-end, from brief through delivery.

 Commission and art-direct external creatives: photographers, illustrators, and motion designers.

 A portfolio that is simply excellent — work that demonstrates mastery of typography, layout, color, and composition across a range of brand contexts.

The Role 
 BeyondTrust is a global leader in privileged access management. Our products provide remote access and privileged control capabilities that are deployed across thousands of enterprise environments worldwide. That makes us a high-value target. Nation-state actors, ransomware operators, and sophisticated threat groups actively target companies like ours—not just to compromise our corporate environment, but to reach the customers who trust our software to protect their most sensitive systems. A compromise of BeyondTrust is a compromise of the privileged access layer inside our customers’ networks. We take that responsibility seriously.
 As a Cyber Defense Engineer on our Cyber Defense Operations team, you will serve as a front-line defender responsible for protecting both BeyondTrust’s enterprise infrastructure and the integrity of the products our customers depend on. You will monitor, investigate, and respond to security events in an environment where the stakes are real and the adversaries are capable. You will work alongside experienced threat hunters, incident responders, and detection engineers in a collaborative team that values sharp analytical thinking over checkbox compliance.
 This team is building toward an AI-augmented operating model. You will be expected to use AI-driven tools in your daily work and to contribute to how we integrate these capabilities into our detection, triage, and response workflows. We are not looking for people who are waiting to be told what to do—we are looking for people who want to build something.
 What You’ll Do 
 Alert Triage & Monitoring 
 Monitor and triage security alerts across SIEM, EDR, and CSPM platforms covering both corporate and product environments.
 Investigate alerts to determine scope, severity, and whether escalation is warranted.
 Leverage AI-assisted triage and enrichment tools to accelerate analysis and reduce mean time to detect.
 Classify, document, and track alerts through the full lifecycle using ticketing and case management systems.
 Incident Response & Investigation 
 Participate in or lead incident response engagements from detection through remediation, including evidence collection, forensic analysis, root cause determination, and stakeholder communication.
 Conduct investigations across SIEM, EDR, CSPM, and cloud-native log sources including identity provider logs, cloud audit trails, and network flow data—spanning both corporate and product infrastructure.
 Execute established IR runbooks across identity, endpoint, cloud, and email investigation workflows.
 Manage or assist with evidence handling, forensic artifact collection, and chain-of-custody procedures.
 Produce clear, decision-ready incident summaries and post-incident reports for both technical and leadership audiences.
 Detection Engineering & Threat Intelligence 
 Contribute to the design, implementation, and tuning of detection rules across SIEM and EDR platforms, with a focus on reducing false positives and closing coverage gaps.
 Translate threat intelligence (CVE advisories, CISA alerts, vendor bulletins, open-source feeds) into actionable detection content, with particular attention to threats targeting privileged access tooling and supply chain attack vectors.
 Help maintain and evolve detection coverage mapped to MITRE ATT&CK.
 Partner with threat hunting peers to validate detection logic through hypothesis-driven hunts.
 AI Integration & Automation 
 Use AI-driven tools for alert triage, enrichment, and investigation as a standard part of daily operations.
 Contribute to the evaluation, integration, and optimization of AI and automation capabilities across the team’s workflows.
 Assist in designing prompts, agent workflows, or LLM-based pipelines that augment analyst capabilities and reduce manual effort.
 Partner with engineering teams to improve log ingestion, data quality, and tool integrations.
 Operational Excellence

 Contribute to and refine IR runbooks, playbooks, and standard operating procedures.

MongoDB powers mission‑critical workloads for customers who expect their data to be durable, highly available, and fast to access. The Storage Execution team builds the core infrastructure that makes those guarantees real.
 We are hiring a Senior Engineering Manager to manage the largely New York-based Storage Execution team. This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is obsessed with customer success, takes the responsibility of durably storing customer data seriously, and has strong empathy for both their team and our users.
 This role can be based remotely in Ontario, Canada.
 About the Storage Execution team
 The Storage Execution team sits at the heart of MongoDB’s Online Transaction Processing (OLTP) team. We own the core transactional read/write path on each node, across both today’s storage engine and a next‑generation cloud-native storage architecture. Our work determines how correct and performant MongoDB is for customers running mission-critical production workloads.
 The team’s responsibilities include:
 Defining and maintaining the internal collection and index APIs used by Replication, Query and Catalog modules, and commands for local reads and writes, plus the transaction and durability primitives that govern visibility, conflict resolution and crash recovery
 Integrating the next generation of MongoDB’s storage architecture into the server in a way that is predictable for other teams, scales with cloud elasticity, and preserves the performance and safety of the classic configuration
 Improving transaction processing speed and semantics of both single shard and cross-shard transactions
 Owning index builds and schema‑level storage operations (build/rebuild, cleanup, resumability) and ensuring they behave well for large, highly available clusters running write-heavy workloads
 Building validation, diagnostics, and storage‑focused test infrastructure to catch durability issues early and keep the system trustworthy at scale
 Partnering with neighboring teams on flow control, prioritization and load-shedding to stay within resource limits, protecting durability and availability at the cluster level without starving critical operations
 What you’ll do
 Lead, grow and manage a New York–based team of 8 to 10 engineers; ensure clear expectations, high standards, and healthy, sustainable execution
 Own the team’s roadmap across durability, availability, performance, and developer productivity, in partnership with OLTP leadership and Product Management
 Manage customer escalations involving storage behavior and durability; work directly with Support, Atlas, and other server teams to reproduce, root‑cause, and resolve issues
 Drive process and tooling improvements that raise engineering velocity and code quality (e.g., ownership, review expectations, customer escalation and build failure practices)
 Partner closely with Replication, Query, Sharding, Catalog & Routing, Storage Engines, and Atlas teams on cross‑team features such as the new storage architecture, availability improvements, and workload management
 Represent Storage Execution in planning, staffing, and calibration; make thoughtful tradeoffs between near‑term deliverables, longer‑term availability gaps, and platform investments
 Candidate profile

 2+ years managing engineers directly, including hiring, performance management, and coaching across a range of levels
 Willing to work East Coast hours
 Strong proficiency in at least one compiled, statically-typed language such as C++, Rust, or Go; prior C++ and systems programming experience is a plus
 Deep understanding of durability, availability, and performance tradeoffs in distributed systems; experience with replication, consensus, storage engines, or transactional systems is highly desirable
 Demonstrated customer obsession: direct experience working with demanding customers (or customer support / cloud teams) on complex incidents and turning them into clear, outcome‑oriented recommendations
 Proven ability to develop people: mentoring and promoting engineers, managing underperformance directly, and building high‑engagement teams with low regretted attrition
 Comfortable leading multi‑quarter initiatives with multiple stakeholders and using written documents to align teams on design, scope, and tradeoffs
 Success measures

 Built strong relationships with your team and key partner teams
 Taken over team ceremonies, short‑term planning, and on‑call responsibilities
 Co‑led at least one active project and shipped one concrete process improvement

Role context

This role sits on the Product Marketing team and reports to the Director of Product Marketing. You'll be aligned to one or more of our product pillars and work with one to three product managers and their engineers, taking products from alpha through public beta to general availability. You're the translator between what product and engineering build and the language sales and customers use.

The role

You will own how your products reach the market, from first alpha to GA.

 - Plan and run launches for mid-tier (P2) products end to end, and lead a major workstream on our biggest (P1) launches, so sales and customer teams are ready on launch day.

 - Shape messaging, positioning and naming with your product counterpart so technical capabilities land as clear value for both the buyer and the frontline technician.

 - Build the collateral, video scripts and enablement that help reps close faster and help customers adopt what we ship.

 - Partner with Demand Gen on campaign messaging and review what goes to market.

 - Use analytics tools, customer conversations and market research to understand buyers, and own an adoption goal, shared with your product counterpart, that we review every week.

Within six to twelve months, product, sales and marketing should see you as the person to ask about your products. You'll have real autonomy to set strategy with your product counterpart and bring recommendations to your manager. Your priorities will shift each quarter with what the business needs.

About you

Must-haves

 - 2–4 years in product marketing or a closely related role, such as sales enablement, sales or marketing

 - You've taken a product launch from plan to release and can tell us what worked and what didn't

 - You write clearly and present with confidence to sales, product and executive audiences

 - You've worked with go-to-market teams before and after the sale

 - You're comfortable getting hands-on in tools like Tableau, Databricks and Salesforce to check on customers and adoption

 - You see the whole picture: tell you one thing and you can map the many moving parts behind it

 - You welcome feedback, take accountability, and know when to push and when to agree and move on

Nice-to-haves

 - Background in manufacturing, industrial or other asset-intensive industries

 - Experience marketing B2B software or AI products

We offer

Your work shows up in the physical world. What we ship keeps factories, fleets and campuses running, and when it works, a technician goes home on time. You're joining a product the industry already loves, now part of Autodesk, with the scale of a global public company pointed at the problem we were already solving. The seat is early, not inherited: the team is small enough that you can name the parts of the launch process you own. And operations is new ground inside Autodesk, so the people who join now have real room to grow.

Values and how we work

We reward output and promote quickly when people deliver. Product marketing here means navigating strong opinions from product, sales and marketing, because everyone cares about the work. We look for people who are smart, humble and optimistic: open to feedback, easy to work with, and honest about what didn't go to plan.
